semantic_fidelity.reason: CDU controller and PDUs and their OOB links are disclosed but absent; physical and host-location qualifiers and SFTP are not visibly spelled out; exporter label owner is visually misleading. Paid components are absent and four direct API paths are visible.

arrow_traceability.reason: OOB has three distinct taps, not the explicitly requested one split. The exporter label sits beside the other port; no unambiguous-placement impossibility was recorded. Individual API routes remain traceable despite the bridge.

layout_fit.reason: All four final views fit pinned 77x47 natural; nevertheless the split does not provide complete source coverage, and v4 has a visually misleading edge-label placement. One v3 bridge is disclosed; no evidence establishes that it is avoidable without sacrificing content.

conceptual_grouping_color.reason: ANSI shows related hues within each declared conceptual group, no group border, and related members near one another; no source-defined tier ordering is contradicted. v1 device row spans bands, a documented spatial tradeoff, not itself a hue failure.

category_fit.reason: Under the round-11 softened criterion the closest source-backed shape is placement-planes; named family and evidence exist, secondary fan/chain habits are visible, and the shared row and three-tap deviation are recorded with reasons. This does not waive the separate explicit one-split or completeness gates.
category_fit.evidence_line: The source is two weakly-connected worlds joined by one shared wire: the OOB LAN is 'a SEPARATE PHYSICAL ETHERNET NETWORK ... usually air-gapped from the data plane' (line 277) that reaches every BMC while the in-band software (GPU Operator -> DCGM -> driver/Fabric Manager) has no link to it at all — the source explicitly forbids the one edge that would join them ('Never draw OOB -> DCGM', line 277, and 'no line from OOB reaches DCGM'). Inside the first world sits the source-named bus: 'one arrow that's coming out from out-of-band LAN ... split in exactly one spot' (line 284).

animation.reason: The source requests a static software-placement explanation and never requests animation; the case manifest marks animation optional. Five frames at both sizes show no animation; no dynamic cycle is required.

findings.description: Defect: CDU controller and PDUs and their OOB connections are source-listed but deliberately dropped. One-split request is binding, but it does not authorize deleting endpoints; record or another view could preserve coverage.
Defect: the source requires exactly one split, but bus visibly has three separate taps. An engine limitation and documented rationale support category_fit, not waiver of explicit traceability.

Defect: serves :9400 is adjacent to the right-hand driver route, not the left-hand exporter route, making ownership misleading; checker reports zero ambiguous. No recorded unambiguous-placement impossibility for this view.
Defect: SSH/SFTP is shortened to SSH; SFTP is not visible. SSH does not explicitly identify the file-transfer protocol stated in the source.

Defect: diagram does not label management-node or compute-host residency, physical Ethernet/OOB details, or Prometheus. Group names in JSON are not rendered; prose metadata is not a substitute for visual placement.
Defect: one visible v3 bridge is distinguishable but degrades simplicity. Avoidability is not proved by the preserved attempts, so it is not independently used to fail crossing-minimization.

Evidence gap: metadata cases_sha256 e69179…8672b… conflicts with actual e69179…8692b…; one earlier rejected draft input was overwritten, so recorded hash 680164… cannot be verified from its path. Raw output hashes are preserved and validator passes.
